gen-irish-grover-gf-noto-sans-tagbanwa: Noto Sans Tagbanwa fills most of its line height with open curves and clear gaps, a plain sans that never crowds itself. Irish Grover just adds sturdy, tall-bodied words on top.
gen-irish-grover-gf-noto-sans-tai-le: Playful and a bit wobbly, Irish Grover gives its words sturdy height and gently shifting weight around every bowl. And Noto Sans Tai Le, with strokes that taper out before touching, is the quiet foil.
gen-irish-grover-gf-noto-sans-tai-tham: Noto Sans Tai Tham packs its lowercase up toward the capital line. Its round letters stay clearly open, so a long passage would feel dense yet easy to enter, while Irish Grover's thick strokes lead the eye above without taking over.
gen-irish-grover-gf-noto-sans-tai-viet: Chunky, bouncy, and friendly. Irish Grover swells and eases in thickness, while Noto Sans Tai Viet keeps short ascenders and a tall x-height, so a long passage would run smoothly underneath.
gen-irish-grover-gf-noto-sans-takri: Irish Grover has a modest thick-and-thin rhythm across each word. Noto Sans Takri sits beneath it with generously unclosed round letters and a high-waisted lowercase, so the two share the page comfortably.
gen-irish-grover-gf-noto-sans-tamil: Irish Grover shifts its weight only slightly, like a stretched rubber cord, giving tall, sturdy words a fun, organic feel. Noto Sans Tamil then reads large and open, with terminals stopping far from the stem.
gen-irish-grover-gf-noto-sans-tamil-supp: Noto Sans Tamil Supplement has round forms like open parentheses and a middle band so tall that lines look stocky. Irish Grover is the one for showy, shimmering headings; this sans does the steady text work.
gen-irish-grover-gf-noto-sans-tangsa: Noto Sans Tangsa opens its round letters wide and keeps short ascender stems on tall lowercase bodies, which makes text feel inviting. Irish Grover, drawn as if with a barely tilted nib, is the one with attitude.
gen-irish-grover-gf-noto-sans-tc: Approachable from the first word, Noto Sans TC has large open counters and curves that flare outward. Irish Grover is best at a subtle thick-and-thin cadence in sturdy headings, while this sans is best at plain, easy text.
gen-irish-grover-gf-noto-sans-telugu: Sturdy, tall, and a little cheeky, Irish Grover shades its weight gently along each curve. And Noto Sans Telugu, a plain sans with a high-set midline, lets big, short headings do the talking.
